title: Voynich manuscript
caveat: These are questions about the material that can be measured before anyone proposes a reading. Answering all of them would not decipher the script; it would make a later claim testable. Nothing here is a reading, and no probability of decipherment is assigned.

lay.tagline: A 15th-century illustrated book in a script nobody can read.
lay.summary: The Voynich manuscript is a book of about 240 pages held at Yale, written in an unknown script and full of drawings of plants, stars and bathing figures. Its vellum has been carbon dated to the early 1400s. Nobody knows whether it hides a real language, a cipher or no meaning at all. We have not proposed a reading. The plan is to measure first how much the statistics change when you change how the script is transcribed.
lay.what_it_is: The script uses perhaps 20 to 30 distinct signs, written in what look like words. Researchers turn it into Roman letters using schemes such as EVA, but those letters are labels for shapes, not sounds, and different schemes split the signs differently.
lay.what_we_found: The declared statistics survive the transcription change: between the two independent EVA transcriptions, glyph frequency ranks agree at 0.999, bigrams at 0.965, and word tokens at 0.901 on 5,013 shared loci, at or above the metric's own resampling ceiling. What differs is segmentation: 34,354 against 36,441 tokens for the same glyph content. No conclusion about language or meaning is drawn.
lay.whats_next: Declare the segmentation choices and measure the range of the statistics under each, with shuffled controls, keeping ten whole folios unseen for testing.

faq.q: Has the Voynich manuscript been deciphered?
faq.a: No. Many readings have been announced; none has been shown to work on pages its author did not use to build it.
It is not settled. The vellum is old, but that does not tell us whether the text means anything.

researcher.summary: Beinecke MS 408. Transliteration ZL 3b (IVTFF 2.0, 13 May 2025) from voynich.nu, to be compared with a second independently authored transliteration. Planned statistics: sign n-grams of orders 1 to 4, token lengths and line-position effects under each declared segmentation, with at most 2,000 seeded nulls preserving word lengths or line lengths, and 10 reserved folios.

statuses.closed-with-power: Answered with a control: measured on a frozen corpus, with a solved or synthetic control showing the method works.
statuses.tested-without-power: Measured without a control: a number exists, but no control shows what it would look like if the answer were different.
statuses.open: Open: proposed here, not yet measured.

families.family: Do the statistics survive a change of transcription?
families.evidence: Measured 20 October 2026 on the 5,013 worded loci shared by ZL 3b and IT 2a outside ten reserved whole folios. Spearman rank correlation over shared types: glyph frequency 0.999, bigrams 0.965, trigrams 0.937, quadgrams 0.915, word tokens 0.901. Glyph totals match within 218 of 184,310; the files split 34,354 and 36,441 tokens (6.1 percent), so the residue is segmentation, not the statistics. Controls: the within-file half-split resampling baseline is 0.73 for word tokens and 0.84 to 1.00 for the rest, so the cross-transcription agreement is at or above the metric's own ceiling; a planted cyclic relabelling of the ten most frequent EVA characters of IT drops bigram agreement to 0.40, trigrams to 0.10, quadgrams to -0.07 and words to 0.26, margins of 0.56 or more; planted miniature files control the pipeline itself. Nothing follows about language or meaning.

families.family: Do they survive a change of word segmentation?
families.evidence: Not measured. The measured 6.1 percent token difference for the same glyph content is this family's opening fact.
families.next: Declare the segmentation choices and recompute the declared statistics under each on the shared loci, reporting the range, not the best case.

families.family: Does the text predict unseen folios better than shuffled text?
families.evidence: Not measured. Ten whole folios reserved 20 October 2026, by seed-keyed hash, statistics-blind: f87r, f96v, f95r2, f68v1, f32v, f106r, f67r1, f36r, f82v, f24r.
families.next: Compare held-out prediction of the reserved folios against word-length and line-length preserving nulls.

families.family: Is it a simple cipher of a known language?
families.evidence: Out of domain for the A to Z engine; not tested here.
families.next: Only after the transcription questions: test a declared cipher model on synthetic Voynich-length controls first.
